score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 6 major vendors (BookYourData, ITNow Technologies, AverickMedia, DataCaptive, LakeB2B, InfoGlobalData) currently selling mortgage broker and loan officer databases ranging from 37K to 114K+ records with commercial pricing models. Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) mortgage technology vendors (Encompass by ICE, Calyx Point, Byte Software, Blend, SimpleNexus) selling loan origination systems (LOS), point-of-sale platforms, pricing engines, and document automation tools at $200-$800/month per loan officer — mortgage tech vendors pay $5,000-$12,000/year for targeted MLO marketing lists to acquire customers with $2,400-$9,600/year LTV; (2) CRM and lead management platforms (Velocify, Mortgage CRM, Lead Pilot, Surefire) selling specialized mortgage lead nurturing, automated email drip campaigns, and borrower relationship management tools at $150-$500/month per user; (3) continuing education (CE) and NMLS renewal course providers selling mandatory federal and state-required courses — all mortgage loan originators must complete 8 hours of NMLS-approved CE annually (3 hours federal law, 2 hours ethics, 2 hours non-traditional mortgage products, plus 1 hour elective) to maintain NMLS license, creating recurring $100-$300/year spend per MLO; and (4) mortgage lead generation platforms, realtor partnership networks, and mortgage marketing agencies targeting purchase mortgage originators and refinance specialists who spend $500-$5,000/month on borrower lead acquisition. The NMLS Consumer Access database (www.nmlsconsumeraccess.org) is the authoritative public registry maintained by the Conference of State Bank Supervisors (CSBS) containing all state-licensed mortgage loan originators, mortgage companies, mortgage brokers, and branches across all participating states. Data includes MLO full name, NMLS ID number, company affiliation, branch location, license status (active, inactive, expired, withdrawn), state licenses held, license issue/expiration dates, and employment history. Zero PII — all professional NMLS credential data under federal SAFE Act requirements and state mortgage lending laws. Engineering lift is moderate: NMLS Consumer Access provides searchable interface but no bulk download API; would require state-by-state scraping or API integration if available, deduplication of multi-state license holders, normalization of company affiliations and license statuses. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell custom lists or annual subscriptions, leaving a clear gap for a one-time $99-$149 CSV. Audience size is substantial: over 400,000 NMLS-registered mortgage professionals nationwide (including loan officers, mortgage brokers, branch managers), creating a TAM of 8,000+ potential B2B buyers across mortgage tech, CRM, CE providers, and lead generation verticals. Score is 8 due to validated strong willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors, confirmed authoritative public data via NMLS Consumer Access under federal SAFE Act transparency mandates, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, large MLO population (400K+), and four distinct B2B buyer segments with proven purchasing behavior in mortgage technology, compliance, and marketing markets.

data_wanted: The NMLS Consumer Access database (www.nmlsconsumeraccess.org) maintained by the Conference of State Bank Supervisors (CSBS) and State Regulatory Registry LLC (SRR) is the authoritative public registry of all mortgage professionals licensed under the federal Secure and Fair Enforcement for Mortgage Licensing Act (SAFE Act). No authentication required for public lookup. Key fields per NMLS record: mortgage loan originator (MLO) full name (first, middle initial, last), unique NMLS ID number (permanent 6-8 digit identifier assigned to each individual), current mortgage company affiliation and employer NMLS company ID, branch location (street address, city, state, ZIP where MLO operates), license status (active, inactive, expired, withdrawn, suspended, revoked), state licenses held (MLOs can be licensed in multiple states; list all jurisdictions), original license issue date, current expiration/renewal date, license type (state-licensed MLO vs. federally registered MLO for depository institutions), employment history with previous mortgage companies and date ranges, and any public enforcement actions or license revocations. Target all active and inactive (but not permanently revoked) NMLS registrations. Scope to individual mortgage loan originators and mortgage brokers — exclude mortgage company entity records (available separately). Approximately 400,000 NMLS-registered mortgage professionals nationwide as of 2026 (note: many MLOs hold licenses in 5-10 states simultaneously due to multi-state lending operations, but each individual has one unique NMLS ID). Target output: 400K rows, one per NMLS ID. Data is 100% public per federal SAFE Act Section 1512 which mandates public access to MLO licensing information, and state mortgage lending statutes requiring transparency in mortgage professional licensing.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Four distinct buyer segments with validated purchasing behavior and high LTV justification. (1) Mortgage technology vendors: loan origination systems generate $200-$800/month per MLO in recurring subscription revenue ($2,400-$9,600/year customer LTV); vendors routinely pay $5,000-$12,000/year for targeted MLO marketing lists, making a $149 one-time CSV deliver 33×-80× cost savings. A single acquired LOS customer yields 16×-64× ROI. (2) CRM platforms: mortgage-specialized CRMs charge $150-$500/month per user ($1,800-$6,000/year LTV); vendors pay $3,000-$8,000/year for broker prospect lists, so a $149 CSV provides 20×-53× cost savings. (3) CE providers: all MLOs must complete 8 hours of NMLS CE annually to maintain license, creating mandatory recurring spend of $100-$300/year per originator; CE vendors pay $2,000-$5,000/year for MLO marketing lists, making a $149 CSV deliver 13×-33× cost savings. A single CE customer yields moderate recurring revenue. (4) Lead generation platforms: mortgage originators spend $500-$5,000/month on borrower leads ($6,000-$60,000/year); lead vendors and marketing agencies charge $2,000-$10,000/month retainers and need MLO prospect databases for outbound BD — a single retained client yields 13×-67× ROI. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $1,000 (all existing vendors sell custom lists or annual access, not one-time CSV downloads) combined with validated commercial pricing creates a strong low-price entry wedge. NMLS Consumer Access is the definitive authoritative source under federal SAFE Act mandate, ensuring data quality and completeness that commercial vendors cannot match without scraping the same public database.
